metadata.description: A network interface in any of its forms: a physical port, a virtual interface, a passthrough, a partition derived from a physical NIC (an SR-IOV VF, a VLAN or macvlan sub-interface), or a composite built from member interfaces (a bond, a bridge). A Base by the Base test (CLS-002): Redfish NetworkAdapter/NetworkPort and the RFC 8343 interface model abstract over all of them, so an interface is one deliverable every host, hypervisor and switch provider realizes; `device_class` says which form. One type therefore carries the whole host interface stack as a traversable tree (physical NICs → bond → bridge → sub-interfaces), serves switch ports too (contained by a NetworkSwitch), and links host NIC to switch port through the LLDP-discovered `connects_to` adjacency.

device_class.description: Device realization (common-elements.md §7): `physical` (a port), `virtual` (virtio, veth), `passthrough`, `partition` (an SR-IOV VF or a VLAN/macvlan sub-interface; set `parent_device`), `aggregate` (a bond) or `bridge`; the last two name their members in `lower_layer`.

partition_mechanism.description: How a partition is carved, when `device_class` is partition: `sr-iov`, `vlan`, `macvlan`, `ipvlan`.

aggregation.description: Bond parameters (IEEE 802.1AX), when `device_class` is aggregate; the members are the `lower_layer` references.

mode.description: Bond mode. 802.3ad = dynamic LACP link aggregation (requires a matching switch LAG); active-backup = failover only. Linux-bonding vocabulary; 802.3ad names IEEE 802.1AX.

lacp_rate.description: Only when mode=802.3ad: LACPDU transmit rate.

miimon.description: MII link-monitoring interval in milliseconds; 0 disables (Linux-bonding vocabulary, like the mode names).

xmit_hash_policy.description: Tx load-balancing hash, e.g. layer2 | layer2+3 | layer3+4 (modes 802.3ad / balance-xor).

min_links.description: Minimum aggregated links for the bond to be considered up.

bridge.description: Software L2 bridge parameters (IEEE 802.1Q), when `device_class` is bridge; the bridged ports are the `lower_layer` references.

vlan_filtering.description: 802.1Q per-port VLAN filtering on the bridge (false = a plain trunk bridge that passes all tags transparently).

identity.description: Instance discriminators: MAC, PCI address, port name.

location.description: PCIe slot / BDF / port designation within the parent (Redfish PhysicalLocation). Primary discriminator; for a VF/sub-interface, its index/name.

mac_address.description: MAC address (Redfish Ethernet MACAddress) — globally unique interface identity.

role.description: Semantic usage, e.g. mgmt | storage | tenant | trunk.

vlan_id.description: An observed VLAN tag recorded by discovery; a convenience, not authoritative. Membership is `vlan_memberships`, and resolution promotes a raw tag into it.

vlan_memberships.description: The port's VLAN membership set (802.1Q): each entry references an existing VLAN and declares its mode. A trunk carries one native plus N tagged; an access port one. Each membership is also a `references` edge to the VLAN.

network_vlan_ref.description: Reference to VLAN — the VLAN this membership tags. Common-elements Reference shape (handle string or {uuid, handle} object); resolvable and policy-walkable, never an opaque string.

mode.description: native = the untagged PVID (at most one per port); tagged = a tagged member (802.1Q).

mac_address.description: Realized MAC address (also a discriminator in identity).

relationships.name: host
relationships.description: The host the physical NIC is installed in.

relationships.name: guest
relationships.description: For virtual / passthrough / partition, the guest the interface is presented to.

relationships.name: switch
relationships.description: For a switch port: the switch it belongs to. Same type serves host NICs and switch ports — the §27 Identity block (location = the port designation, e.g. 'Port 14') distinguishes instances.

parent_device — the ONE physical NIC this passthrough/partition (SR-IOV VF, VLAN/macvlan sub-interface) is derived from (1→N). REQUIRED when device_class is passthrough or partition (common-elements §7).
relationships.name: parent_device
relationships.adopted_from: RFC 8343 lower-layer-if (declared refinement: the 1-to-N slice direction)

relationships.description: lower_layer — the MEMBER interfaces this composite is built from (N→1): a bond's aggregated NICs (802.1AX) or a bridge's ports (802.1Q). The inverse of parent_device; RFC 8343 lower-layer-if. REQUIRED when device_class is aggregate or bridge (common-elements §7).
relationships.name: lower_layer

relationships.description: connects_to (renamed from connected_to when relation names were adopted from standards, common-elements §9) — the PEER termination point this physical interface is linked to (host NIC ↔ switch port; switch ↔ switch uplink). Symmetric adjacency, declared once (either end). Discovered via IEEE 802.1AB LLDP (Chassis ID + Port ID name the peer); a mismatch between declared cabling and the LLDP-observed neighbor is drift (OBS-001). RFC 8345 models this as a link between two termination-points — promote to a first-class link entity only if links ever need their own attributes (cable id, patch panel); until then the reference keeps surface area minimal (common-elements §7a).
relationships.name: connects_to
vlan_membership
relationships.description: The VLAN(s) this port is a member of (see spec.vlan_memberships); each carries a mode (native/tagged). The port references the shared VLAN objects rather than duplicating the id.

adopts.role: network-interface component vocabulary (NetworkAdapter/NetworkPort/NetworkDeviceFunction: MAC, speed, MTU)
interface-stacking vocabulary — a composite interface (bond/bridge) references its member interfaces via lower_layer (RFC 8343 lower-layer-if)
software L2 bridge + VLAN vocabulary (device_class=bridge, bridge.vlan_filtering, vlan_id)
relation vocabulary — connects_to peer-adjacency relation name (common-elements §9)

adopts.standard_name: Station and Media Access Control Connectivity Discovery (LLDP)
adopts.role: connects_to peer-discovery vocabulary (host NIC <-> switch port adjacency)

context.purpose: Models every kind of network interface — physical NIC, virtual NIC, SR-IOV slice, bond, bridge, and switch port — as one traversable device type.
context.plain_description: One network interface, of any kind: device_class says whether it is a physical NIC, a fully virtual interface (virtio/veth), a whole-NIC passthrough, a partition carved from one physical NIC (an SR-IOV VF or VLAN sub-interface, pointing up at its parent), or a composite built from many members (a bond or a bridge, pointing down at its members). The same type also serves switch ports. Identity facts — the MAC address (`mac_address`), location, serial, model — nest under the `identity` block, not at the top level. A physical interface carries a connects_to edge to its discovered peer port, which is what makes host → NIC → switch port → switch a walkable path. VLAN membership is declared by referencing VLAN records, never by retyping raw tags.
use_when: You need the full host interface stack — NICs, bond, bridge, sub-interfaces — as records whose parent/member links mirror reality.
You need host-NIC-to-switch-port cabling (LLDP-discovered) in the graph for impact analysis.
You need a port's VLAN membership (native/tagged) declared against shared VLAN records.
not_for: The attachment point guests plug into — VirtualNetwork; a bridge here is the device, the VirtualNetwork is the workload-facing network on top of it.
The desired configuration applied to an interface (addressing, routes, DNS) — ConnectionProfile configures the device this type inventories.
The VLAN segment itself — VLAN; interfaces are members of a segment, they don't define it.
works_with: Machine.BareMetalHost / NetworkSwitch — what contains the interface (host NIC vs switch port).
NetworkInterface — parent_device, lower_layer, and connects_to: partition parentage, bond/bridge membership, cable adjacency.
VLAN — the segments the port is a member of.
ConnectionProfile — the declarative config realized onto this interface.
